cards.explanation: The answer is that Nahash once showed David kindness. David says, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” Nahash was the king of the Ammonites who just died, and Hanun is his son. David is paying kindness back with kindness. That's a man who remembers who was good to him.

The answer is that they say David's servants came to spy out the land and overthrow it. The princes of the Ammonites ask Hanun, “Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?” David sent comforters, and the princes called them spies. Hanun is the new king, and he has some very loud voices in his ear. Friends, I've seen a recipe get doubted less.

The answer is False. Hanun, the new king of the Ammonites, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away. David's men came to console him and left humiliated. That one's a heavy moment, and I think it stings to read.

The answer is that David sends messengers to meet his men. When someone told David what happened, he sent messengers to meet them, since the text says the men had been thoroughly humiliated. David told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.” He didn't send them back to Hanun.

The answer is until their beards have grown back. David tells his men, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.” Jericho is a city, and that's where they wait. Beards grow on their own schedule, friends. I'd know, since my mustache does what it wants.

The answer is chariots and horsemen from Aram. The Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah. Those are Aramean regions. This came after the Ammonites realized they had become a stench to David. That's a lot of silver spent on hired soldiers.

The answer is True. When David heard about the hired army, he sent Joab, his army commander, with the entire army of mighty men. David didn't send a small group. He sent the entire army of mighty men.

The answer is that Joab splits his troops into two groups. Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him. So he selected some of the best men of Israel to face the Arameans, and the rest went under his brother Abishai against the Ammonites. Two fronts, two groups. Joab, David's army commander, split his troops to meet both.

The answer is True. Joab, David's army commander, selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans. The rest went to his brother Abishai against the Ammonites. So Joab's group was the one set against the Arameans.

The answer is that if one side is losing, the other comes to help. Joab tells his brother Abishai that if the Arameans are too strong for him, Abishai will come to his rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for Abishai, Joab will come to his. Each brother covers the other. Two armies, one deal, and whoever gets pressed has help coming.

The answer is that Joab leaves the outcome to the LORD. He ends with, “May the LORD do what is good in His sight.” Right before that he says, “Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God.” He gives it everything he has and leaves the result with the LORD. That's a solid way to head into a fight.

The answer is that the Arameans flee before Joab. Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, and the Arameans fled before him. These were the chariots and horsemen the Ammonites hired with their silver. Friends, I've seen cookies leave a plate slower.

The answer is True. When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai, Joab's brother, and they entered the city. The Ammonites had hired the Arameans, and once the hired help ran, they did too. After that, Joab went back to Jerusalem.

The answer is True. When the report reached David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and advanced toward the Arameans. That's the king leading himself, not just sending a commander. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, was leading the other side.

The answer is that the Arameans flee and Shophach is killed. The Arameans fled before Israel. David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach, the commander of their army. The Arameans had come with a lot, and it didn't hold.
The answer is that they make peace with David and serve him. Hadadezer's subjects saw that Israel had beaten them. So they made peace with David and became subject to him. They chose peace.

The answer is False. Hadadezer's subjects made peace with David and became subject to him, and the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore. The Ammonites had paid a thousand talents of silver to hire Arameans. And now the Arameans wouldn't help.
The answer is False. Joab led out the army, and David remained in Jerusalem. Joab ravaged the land of the Ammonites and came to Rabbah. David was not on the road with them.
The answer is that Joab attacks Rabbah and demolishes it. Joab came to Rabbah, an Ammonite city, and besieged it. Then he attacked Rabbah and demolished it. He started a siege and finished the job.

The answer is gold. The crown was found to weigh a talent of gold, and it was set with precious stones. A talent is a big weight, and this was a whole talent of gold. Friends, my chef's hat is made of cloth and weighs next to nothing.

The answer is on David's own head. David took the crown from the head of the Ammonite king, and it was placed on David's head. It moved from one head to the other. That's a talent of gold changing heads.

The answer is True. David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. The text says he did the same to all the Ammonite cities. It's a heavy part of the story.
